introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Food and Nutrition 2 (0540), ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2026. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Instructions to candidates: ANSWER ANY FOUR QUESTIONS.

You are reminded of the necessity of good English and orderly presentation of work. Tabulate wherever possible and use diagrams where appropriate.
incertitudes: Règle de choix : la page de garde imprime « ANSWER ANY FOUR QUESTIONS » (4 sur 6 questions imprimées), sans section et sans mention « only the first four will be marked ». `groupes` = ["PAPER 2"] et `regles_choix` = parmi 4 sur 6, identiques dans les 6 fichiers.

Sujet scanné de 3 pages (page de garde, questions 1 à 4, questions 5 et 6), lu en image ; aucun schéma ni figure imprimé, donc `figures` vide dans tous les fichiers. Filigranes (gcerevision.com, Kawlo) ignorés. L'en-tête imprimé « Food And Nutrition 2 » est recopié en « Food and Nutrition 2 » dans l'introduction.

Points : chaque question imprime « Total = (25 marks) » ; les points imprimés des sous-questions totalisent bien 25 pour chacune des 6 questions (aucun écart). Pour 2(a), 5(a) et 6(b), `points` de la sous-question est la somme des parties (i) et (ii) imprimées (2+5, 2+5, 3+5).

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées au nombre exact d'éléments demandés. D'autres réponses sont valables pour les questions de liste ; le barème d'un point par élément est une hypothèse (le sujet ne le détaille pas). Aucune teneur nutritive chiffrée n'est avancée, sauf l'énergie d'un gramme de lipide (environ 37 kJ, valeur du programme).

Question 1(e) « mechanical raising agents » : le programme n'en nomme usuellement que deux (l'air et la vapeur), le sujet en demande quatre. Le corrigé donne quatre procédés mécaniques distincts (air par tamisage, par crémage, par fouettage, et vapeur) ; d'autres manuels répondent autrement (battage, pliage, laminage). À relire par un enseignant de Food and Nutrition.

Faits de cours à relire par un enseignant : les objectifs alimentaires de 5(b) (le sujet n'en impose aucun), les causes de faible production de 5(c) et les points de 6(d) sont des listes de manuel ; plusieurs autres réponses seraient acceptées.

Fautes d'impression du sujet recopiées telles quelles : « five (5) importance » au singulier (1d, 2a ii, 2d, 4d), « (5marks) », « (8marks) », « Recall three (3) advantages », « Pick out three (3) advantages ... of microwave cooking » sans point final, « Outline three (3) advantages and two (2) disadvantages of boiling » sans point final, « Define invitation ».

questions.enonce_markdown:
i. Define invitation.

(2 marks)

ii. Select five (5) ways to respond to an invitation.

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**i. Definition (2 marks).** An invitation is a request, spoken or written, asking a person or a group of people to come to an event such as a meal, a party, a wedding or a ceremony.

**ii. Five ways to respond to an invitation (1 mark each).** The reply should be made quickly, and it should say clearly whether the guest will come or not.

1. **A formal written reply accepting** the invitation (a letter or the reply card, "RSVP").
2. **A written reply declining politely**, with thanks and a short reason.
3. **A telephone call** to the host, to accept or to decline.
4. **An e-mail or text message** (for example by phone) to the host, for an informal invitation.
5. **A reply in person** (verbally), when the guest meets the host.

(A guest who accepts must arrive on time, and a thank-you note may be sent after the event.)

**Dietary goals** are recommendations about the way a person should eat in order to stay healthy. Six dietary goals (1 mark each):

1. **Eat a variety of foods** from all the food groups to get all the nutrients.
2. **Balance the energy eaten with the energy used** in order to keep a healthy body weight.
3. **Eat less fat**, especially fried and animal fats, to reduce the risk of overweight and heart disease.
4. **Eat less sugar** and sugary foods and drinks, which also cause tooth decay.
5. **Eat less salt**, which helps to prevent high blood pressure.
6. **Eat more fruits, vegetables and fibre-rich foods** (whole cereals, beans) and drink enough clean water.

(Other correct point: take alcohol in moderation or not at all.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
State and explain three (3) reasons for the causes of low food production.

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Three causes of low food production (1 mark for the cause and 1 mark for the explanation, so 2 marks each):

1. **Poor farming methods.** Many farmers use simple tools (hoe and cutlass), local seeds and no fertiliser, so the yield per hectare is low and the farm stays small.
2. **Bad weather and natural disasters.** Drought, floods or irregular rains destroy crops and reduce the harvest.
3. **Pests and diseases.** Insects, birds, rats and plant diseases destroy crops in the field and in the store, so a large part of the harvest is lost.

(Other correct causes: poor soils and lack of fertilisers, lack of money or credit, poor roads and storage, drift of young people to towns, and insecurity.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Enumerate six (6) ways through which food can be contaminated.

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Food is **contaminated** when it receives harmful germs (bacteria, viruses), dirt or chemicals. Six ways (1 mark each):

1. **By the hands of food handlers** who have not washed their hands, or who are sick or have septic wounds.
2. **By pests and animals** - flies, cockroaches, rats and pets walk on food and leave germs.
3. **By dirty utensils, equipment and work surfaces** that were not washed properly.
4. **By raw food touching cooked food** (cross-contamination), for example the same knife or board used for raw meat and for cooked food.
5. **By unsafe water** used for washing or cooking food.
6. **By dust, coughing or sneezing over food**, or by leaving food uncovered; and by chemicals such as insecticides or cleaning liquids kept near the food.
